metadata.sampling_strategy: Stratified sample: 50 high-confidence COMPANY_COMMITMENT, 50 high-confidence PRACTICE, 50 high-confidence USER_CONTROL, 50 AMBIGUOUS/low-confidence/disagreement cases. 100 from OPPT corpus, 100 from OPP-115 corpus. Company diversity enforced (143 unique companies). Random seed=42 for reproducibility.
metadata.annotation_guidelines: Gold labels assigned based on speech act theory (Austin 1962, Searle 1976). PRACTICE = assertive speech acts describing what company does with data. COMPANY_COMMITMENT = commissive speech acts where company binds itself to limitations or promises. USER_CONTROL = descriptions of user capabilities, rights, or choices. Key edge case rules: (1) Negated practices ('we do not sell') = COMPANY_COMMITMENT; (2) Epistemic hedges ('we may share') = PRACTICE; (3) Scope disclaimers ('we are not responsible for third parties') = PRACTICE; (4) Security disclaimers ('cannot guarantee') = PRACTICE (disclaimer of limitation, not a promise; corrected 2026-09-01, see corrections); (5) DNT non-response ('does not respond to DNT') = PRACTICE (describes behavior, not privacy-protective promise); (6) User obligations placed by company = PRACTICE.
metadata.annotator: Thomas Brackin (author, CIPP/US). Candidate labels were proposed by Claude Opus 4.6 and each label was adjudicated by the author; single-adjudicator reference set, limitations noted in the paper.

corrections.reason: Draft guideline item (4) labeled security disclaimers as commitments, contradicting the binding-force criterion and prompt edge case 4. Six disclaimer statements (cannot guarantee / cannot promise) corrected. Pre-correction primary-panel accuracy: 185/198 (93.4%), commitment recall 0.857.
